decision_conditions: The proposed development, and the cycle storage in particular, due to its excessive width and depth, would unacceptably increase the built form on the site's front boundary and within the frontage of the house, adding an incongruous form of development where there are no other examples of structures of such scale within the front gardens in the streetscene. The proposed detached storage would appear overly dominant within the frontage of the dwelling to the detriment of the established open character of the frontages in the residential setting. As such, the design of the cycle storage is unacceptable as would result in harm to the character of the dwelling and the Buckhurst Avenue streetscene, contrary to Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Sutton's SPD 4 and SPD 14 'Creating Locally Distinctive Places'.

Due to the close proximity of the cycle and bin stores to the ground floor primary windows of Rooms 1 and 2, the proposed development would result in an adverse impact on the future occupiers of these single aspect rooms in terms of increased noise, disturbance and odour pollution. The proposal would therefore fail to provide good living conditions for future occupiers, contrary to Policy 9 of the Sutton Local Plan and Policy D6 and GG3 of the London Plan 2021.

The proposed loft conversion fails to provide an acceptable standard of internal living conditions for current and future occupiers of Bedroom 5. The proposed additional bedroom would have an internal floor-to-ceiling height that falls substantially short of minimum standard under London's policy, as well as national internal space standards. The proposed new habitable room would restrict circulation space and fail to ensure adequate daylight and ventilation, therefore, the proposal fails to mitigate negative health impacts such as poor ventilation, overheating, or restricted space. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to Policy 9 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policies D6 and GG3 of the London Plan 2021.

Without evidence to the contrary, by way of an on-street parking survey (to Lambeth Methodology) to demonstrate that the surrounding road network can accommodate the potential increased demand for on-street parking from the change of use to a 5-person HMO, it is considered that the proposed parking provision at the site, which is in proximity to two schools, would not be acceptable and the proposal would cause harm in terms of potential parking overspill on the surrounding streets to the detriment of existing on-street parking provision, pedestrian safety and residential amenity, contrary to Policy T6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.
